children: Aerospace and defense stocks fell broadly Tuesday as President Donald Trump raised the prospect of a negotiated end to the U.S. conflict with Iran during an address to the United Nations, while warning that military action could intensify if Tehran refuses to reach an agreement.
V2X
fell about 3.8%, Kratos Defense & Security Solutions
dropped 3.7% and Karman Holdings
declined 3.5%. BAE Systems
was down 2.9%, Northrop Grumman
fell 2.8% and Lockheed Martin
lost 2.7%. General Dynamics
, Huntington Ingalls
, L3Harris Technologies
and RTX
also traded lower.

The declines came as Trump told the UN General Assembly that he expects the United States eventually to reach an agreement with Iran. He said he believes Tehran will make a deal after the U.S. midterm elections on Nov. 3.

Trump's remarks nevertheless offered no assurance that the fighting will end soon. He presented Iran with a choice between reaching an agreement that would allow the country to rebuild and facing renewed U.S. attacks.

The comments underscored the uncertainty surrounding the conflict. Investors have been watching diplomatic developments for indications of how long the war may continue and what that could mean for demand for missiles, interceptors and other military equipment.
Trump also addressed concerns that months of fighting have depleted U.S. weapons inventories. He said the United States has ample munitions and is producing them at unprecedented levels.
Military experts and U.S. allies this year have raised concerns about declining inventories of weapons including Tomahawk cruise missiles, Patriot interceptors and THAAD interceptors.

That issue has significant implications for defense contractors even if hostilities with Iran ease. Rebuilding U.S. inventories could sustain demand for missile systems and other weapons after the conflict ends. The Trump administration has separately emphasized expanding the U.S. defense industrial base and increasing production capacity.
Russia's war in Ukraine

Trump also used his UN address to predict progress toward ending Russia's war in Ukraine. He said the United States was working with Russian and Ukrainian leaders and suggested an agreement could come sooner than expected.
The combination of possible diplomatic progress in Iran and Ukraine offered investors another reason to reassess defense shares that have been sensitive to geopolitical developments.

Still, Trump's comments on Iran were far from a declaration of peace. He warned the United States could launch significantly more destructive attacks if negotiations fail. The administration also called for continued economic pressure on Tehran even as U.S. officials indicated they remained open to diplomacy.

That leaves defense investors weighing two competing forces: the possibility that major conflicts could move toward negotiated settlements and the longer-term need for the United States and its allies to replenish weapons inventories depleted by recent fighting.

title: Defense stocks fall as Trump raises prospect of Iran peace deal at UN
